problem.text: In triangle $ABC$, angles $A$ and $B$ measure $60$ degrees and $45$ degrees, respectively. The bisector of angle $A$ intersects $\overline{BC}$ at $T$, and $AT = 24$. The area of triangle $ABC$ can be written in the form $a + b\sqrt{c}$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive integers, and $c$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. Find $a + b + c$.

steps.title: Where to start: the bisector makes special angles
steps.body: Bisecting the $60^\circ$ angle at $A$ gives two $30^\circ$ angles, and $\angle B = 45^\circ$. Angles of $30^\circ$ and $45^\circ$ are the clue to cut the figure into $30$-$60$-$90$ and $45$-$45$-$90$ triangles, where the known length $AT = 24$ spreads to the other sides. So drop a perpendicular from $T$ to $AB$, meeting it at $H$.

steps.title: Triangle $AHT$ is 30-60-90
steps.body: Triangle $AHT$ has a right angle at $H$ and a $30^\circ$ angle at $A$, and its hypotenuse is $AT = 24$. The sides of a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$.

steps.title: Triangle $THB$ is 45-45-90
steps.body: Triangle $THB$ has a right angle at $H$ and a $45^\circ$ angle at $B$, so it is isosceles and $HB = HT$. This gives the full base $AB = AH + HB$.

steps.title: Find side $AC$
steps.body: To get the height of $ABC$ we need another side. Look at triangle $ATC$: it has $\angle CAT = 30^\circ$ and $\angle C = 75^\circ$.

your_turn.prompt: Find $\angle ATC$. What does it tell you about $AC$?
your_turn.answer: $\angle ATC = 180^\circ - 30^\circ - 75^\circ = 75^\circ = \angle C$, so triangle $ATC$ is isosceles with $AC = AT = 24$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Drop the altitude from $C$ to $AB$, meeting it at $M$. Triangle $ACM$ has a right angle at $M$ and $\angle A = 60^\circ$, so it is $30$-$60$-$90$ with hypotenuse $24$, and $CM = 12\sqrt{3}$. Then
$$[ABC] = \frac{1}{2}\cdot 12\sqrt{3}\cdot(12\sqrt{3}+12) = 216 + 72\sqrt{3}.$$ Here $c = 3$ has no square factor, so $a = 216$, $b = 72$, $c = 3$, and $a + b + c = 291$. The answer is **$291$**.
